rule: Ordinance 86-013 and Decree 86-310 include products prepared by drying. Adopted Order 4736/2002 articles 3–4 require an import permit and origin phytosanitary certificate for covered plant products; article 6 repeats the certificate requirement. The complete annex provides tea conditions for propagation material/seeds, not manufactured drinking tea, and no general manufactured-tea exemption was found. Some other commodities have specific inspection-only conditions. The current Customs summary names certificate controls for chapters 6, 7, 8 and 24.01 but does not settle HS0902 tea. Whether steamed/dried sencha remains in the regulated simple-preparation category is unresolved.
personalMailApplicability: Do not extend a passenger provision to an online postal purchase.
authority: Madagascar official trade portal, plant-protection legislation
remainingQuestion: Which current commodity condition applies to manufactured steamed/dried tea, and is its private postal import exempt from the general permit/certificate pathway?

Independently downloaded and compared the complete 56-page FAO and 55-page German NPPO copies of Order 4736/2002, plus the official PIC-hosted 4-page body. The search title PROJET is stale PDF metadata: all actual texts bear adopted instrument number 4736/2002, date 7 October 2002, and the minister signature attribution. PIC indexes it as a ministerial order. Read the full annex beyond tea propagation; no blanket processed/dried-food exemption was found, but specific milled-rice/grain entries show why an unlisted processed commodity must not automatically receive the propagation conditions. Preserved the unresolved tea classification rather than using the document-title artefact to dismiss the order or claiming that every processed food is exempt.
permitFreeReason: The adopted order is valid evidence of general import controls, but its tea annex concerns propagation material and seeds. Neither the full annex nor the current Customs summary resolves the finished-sencha classification and private-post conditions. No no-document route is established; this is an unresolved classification, not an affirmative tea prohibition.
